source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 in two steps, both run by programs/recipe32.sh, which wrote programs/RECIPE.log. Step 1, profile product (method of Colbourn and Torres-Jimenez 2013, Thm 4.2 / Cor 4.5; programs/pprod.py) of the table's own CA(15; 2, 20, 3) (CA_15_2_20_3_fd13075b, rows 0 and 3, 5 agreements) and our own CA(20; 2, 61, 3) built on 2026-11-09 (programs/CA_20_2_61_3_ingredient.txt, rows 0 and 3, 13 agreements), giving CA(32; 2, 1155, 3). Step 2, column extension at 32 rows with programs/ext2t.c, one column at a time, each new column the best of 200 random columns, then simulated annealing with exact pair counts in which only the new column may change (temperature 0.7, seed 13), and a new column that stays stuck for 200000 moves is drawn again (command ext2t p32_1155.txt 32 1155 0 0 13 1000000 0.7 out/t32f -chain 600 -ntry 200 -kick 200000). The array saved after the 272nd added column, at move 46965623, is this array. Three separate executions (Apple Silicon and x86_64) gave the identical file, see programs/REPLAY.md. Exact check with ca_verify, all column pairs
construction: Profile product of our CA(15; 2, 20, 3) and CA(20; 2, 61, 3), CA(32; 2, 1155, 3), then column extension by simulated annealing to 1427 columns
notes: 32 rows at 1427 columns; the cited 32-row size has 1308 columns; replaces the 1390-column array of smolen-2026-11-t2v3-32rows with a fully replayable one; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start
